svg.text: AC mains → PZEM-004T v3.0 + CT clamp → 2-channel relay → loads, with ESP32 low-voltage control
Everything above the dashed line is live mains. Enclose it. Bench-test on USB first.
LOW-VOLTAGE DC SIDE - 5 V / 3.3 V - SAFE TO PROBE
NEUTRAL - blue - NEVER switched, NEVER through the relay
measures: V · A · W · kWh · Hz · PF
voltage from its AC terminals, current from the CT clamp
P = V × I × PF is computed inside the module
IN = LOW → coil energised → COM-NO closed → load ON
both channels are driven together = one MASTER cut-off
A current transformer: it senses the magnetic field around
ONE conductor, so nothing is cut and the circuit is not broken.
It sits AFTER the Hi-Link / PZEM voltage taps and BEFORE the
relay COM, so it reads load current only - not the meter's own
supply. Relay OFF therefore drives the reading to about 0 A.
WHY THE TAPS SIT BEFORE THE RELAY
Hi-Link and the PZEM voltage terminals are wired upstream of
COM. If they sat after it, switching the relay OFF would cut power
to the ESP32 itself - and it could never switch back ON.
of DC power on the board:
label, not by a long wire
filled dot = the wires are joined
Clamp the CT around ONE live wire. Live + neutral
together cancel out and read about 0 A.
Switch the LIVE conductor, never the neutral.
Earth runs panel → appliance directly: never through
the relay contacts or the PZEM.
Use NO, so a dead ESP32 leaves the load OFF.
Firmware cut-offs: over 1000 W instant, plus a 30 s
